customerCreationPrincipals: Telegram sender identity plus conversational FSM
authorityBoundary.provider: SwapUZ receives source/destination assets, amount, destination address and a generated opaque UUID; the service credential is read by both Relay and bot from an overbroad shared environment bundle.
authorityBoundary.custody: The customer sends assets directly to the provider deposit address and the provider sends to the customer destination; ObsidianExchange does not sign or hold the swap assets, but it creates the provider order and stores both addresses and lifecycle state.
authorityBoundary.statusPageAuthorization: 32-byte-class opaque URL bearer only; possession exposes destination/deposit addresses and a GET also performs provider status I/O plus a local status transition.
authorityBoundary.callbackTrust: Legacy unauthenticated Trocador callback is correlation-only and re-fetches provider state before a forward-only transition; active SwapUZ lifecycle is polled instead and lacks the same recognized-status/forward-only guard.
authorityBoundary.referralMoneyWriter: The bot monitor can invoke ledger-backed referral finalization after a locally observed finished status; this slice did not exercise or re-accept that separate money writer.

criticalFindings: Both customer flows call SwapUZ create-order before inserting a local swap session. Timeout, malformed response, process crash or local insert failure can leave an externally created order with no accepted durable pre-submit attempt or reconciliation record; retry may create another provider order.
The generated UUID is sent to SwapUZ, but deployed evidence contains no accepted provider idempotency/read-back contract proving exact retry or recovery after an ambiguous submit.

SwapUZ maps unknown numeric states to status_<number> and failures to unknown; Relay and the background bot accept any truthy changed value into the local status column without a recognized transition graph. Terminal states are therefore not immutable for this active provider path.

The public /swap/{token} bearer page returns customer destination and provider deposit addresses and performs provider I/O plus a database transition on GET. The token is high entropy and not logged by the route, but there is no authenticated owner binding, expiry, revocation or read-only GET behavior.

The web flow re-fetches limits before create but does not content-bind an explicit quote/expiry/fee preview to a confirmation intent; the Telegram flow displays an estimate, then submits later without re-quoting or binding customer consent to the final provider terms.

Customer copy is internally inconsistent: public/site surfaces advertise approximately 1% while the landing Mini App chip says 2%; the UI does not bind exact provider, network, fee, expiry, refund path or irreversibility before submit.
SwapUZ credential scope is overbroad: Relay, bot, notifier and monitor consume the shared application secret bundle although the target ownership plan calls for a dedicated swap routing worker.

telegramBot.reason: A customer FSM quotes, validates a destination, creates a SwapUZ order, stores the session and later polls status; submit precedes durable intent and quote/transition/recovery controls are unaccepted.

site.reason: Authenticated dashboard plus CSRF creates swaps and lists owner-scoped history, but the resulting status page is an unexpired bearer URL and GET mutates state after provider I/O.

miniApp.reason: The deployed Mini App only advertises a Swap 2% chip and has no swap workflow or explicit safe handoff; it conflicts with the approximately 1% site/bot claim.

admin.reason: Filament exposes a read-only swap resource, including bearer token and both addresses, behind the general admin/MFA contour; status/provider filters are stale relative to deployed SwapUZ values.

api.reason: Relay exposes dashboard create, bearer status and legacy Trocador callback routes plus repository/provider adapters, but no versioned swap-intent API, durable attempt, accepted idempotency or ambiguous-submit recovery exists.

native.reason: No native swap request/status handoff exists; any future surface must keep local signing authority and provider credentials separate.

limitations: Relay, bot and deployed swap repository differ from checkout, so production claims are bound to exact deployed hashes rather than inferred from current checkout revisions.
No authenticated customer/admin route, bearer swap page, callback, provider endpoint, database row or referral finalizer was exercised.
No customer identifier, address, token, provider credential or provider response was read; runtime status was limited to service metadata and a public root observation.

An independent reviewer accidentally caused one provider secret value to appear in its private tool output while searching environment names. The value is intentionally omitted; the credential requires external rotation, but no replacement credential or provider-console access exists in this slice.
Static source proves reachable code shape, not provider-side idempotency or legal/terms readiness; both remain unproven.

Existing rows already holding unknown, status_* or other non-canonical states require explicit manual reconciliation before any rollout; the fail-closed candidate intentionally does not auto-promote poisoned legacy state.

independentReviews.finding: After catching and correcting a monitor-scope import regression, strict decoding plus terminal immutability closes the demonstrated SwapUZ finished-to-unknown-to-finished duplicate-credit chain; broader lifecycle blockers remain.
Strict typed decoding, caller binding, honest legacy-state handling and focused assertions are sufficient for the narrow candidate, while deployed SWAPS remains PARTIAL_NOT_ACCEPTED.

Telegram/site/provider/admin reachability is real, but six-surface product and money-authority acceptance fails on persistence order, status integrity, bearer privacy, provider custody/fees and reconciliation.
